iterations.notes: all three beats present and in order; Marcos s answer word for word the outline s; the ending shows the love rather than naming it; M2 lands as love with the cost to Marcos visible, though asserted twice in narrator voice as well as dramatised.

findings.quote: He met his eyes-the grey ones that had been waiting for this moment since before he was born. Neither of them looked away.
findings.claim: The outline asks for him seeing only love there; with the naming clause cut, the love now depends entirely on the reader s inference.
findings.fix: restore a shorter concrete signal of the love without the abstraction

iterations.notes: beats unchanged and still in order. The critic raised one HIGH finding its scoring rule does not charge: cutting the clause that named what he saw in his grandfather s eyes has made the love implicit rather than demonstrated, and it judged the emotional content materially reduced. ORCHESTRATOR ARBITRATION: this is in direct opposition to the prose critic, which charged that same clause as the book telling a child what to feel at the moment it should show him - the identical disagreement these two critics had over chapter 3 s ending. The prose reading was followed and the outline critic s objection is recorded open rather than acted on. A reader deciding which was right should read the last two lines of chapter 8 and judge.
